title: Yannic Damm
text:
I am an applied economist and doctoral researcher at the Institute for Food and Resource Economics (ILR) at the University of Bonn.
My research focuses on land-use change, environmental policies, and impact evaluation, particularly in the Brazilian Amazon. I also occasionally write tutorials on spatial data analysis in R.

title: Research
text: My research interests lie at the intersection of environmental economics, development economics, and impact evaluation. I primarily study land-use change, environmental policy enforcement, and the socio-economic and health co-benefits of conservation policies, with a strong regional focus on the Brazilian Amazon.

Media & Outreach

Podcast: Rainforest conservation is bad for the economy!? (2026)
A discussion on the relationship between rainforest conservation and the economic, health outcomes, and crime. With Gustavo Magalhães de Oliveira on the University of Bonn’s Hypothese podcast.
News Article: Our paper “Health Benefits of Reduced Deforestation in the Brazilian Amazon” in Communications Earth & Environment gathered some media attention. There was a press release by the University of Bonn and later the publication was covered by the Deutsche Welle and Brazilian news outlets O Globo and Agência Pública.
Blogpost: Can public scrutiny make supply chains more sustainable? (2024)
A summary of our paper “Beyond Deforestation Reductions: Public Disclosure, Land-Use Change and Commodity Sourcing” in World Development on the evidence from Brazilian municipalities which suggests that reputational risk exposure can reduce deforestation and intensify agriculture. With Elías Cisneros & Jan Börner on the United Nations Industrial Development Organization’s Industrial Analytics Platform.
